events.title: Ada language standardized
events.summary: On February 17, 1983, ANSI approved [Ada] — a language the U.S. Defense Department required for safety-critical software like aircraft and weapons systems.
events.about: [Ada] was built for large, high-reliability projects — avionics, defense, and embedded control. It enforced strict typing, organized code into modules, and supported running multiple tasks safely in parallel. Boeing, Airbus, and military contractors still maintain millions of lines of [Ada] where failure is not an option.

narrative.whyChosen: [Ada] was the first programming language standardized under a strict government procurement mandate — reliability was the goal, not speed of hacking.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved that a language could be designed upfront for safety and long-term maintenance on huge government-scale projects.
narrative.problemSolved: Defense projects used hundreds of incompatible languages and tools; the Pentagon wanted one portable standard every contractor could be required to use.
